package_info.why_malicious: The package contains code that, upon installation, collects sensitive files such as SSH keys and Kubernetes configuration, fingerprints the system, and exfiltrates this data to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. The package impersonates legitimate libraries and uses deceptive metadata to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system fingerprinting information (username, hostname), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses highly sensitive files (SSH private key, Kubernetes config) and sends them to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not access or exfiltrate user SSH keys or Kubernetes configs during installation. Legitimate packages may collect telemetry, but not sensitive credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise endpoint management tools may collect system info with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Network exfiltration to hardcoded external domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the obfuscated code performs the same actions as the plaintext version: reads sensitive files, fingerprints the system, and exfiltrates data to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent, and the code still accesses and exfiltrates sensitive files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate code that accesses user credentials or system files, especially in postinstall scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection, but not for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: References to sensitive file paths and external domains
Same data exfiltration logic as plaintext variant

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., @am-fe/hooks or @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable).
Postinstall script executes, collecting sensitive files (SSH key, Kubernetes config) and system fingerprinting data.
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Network requests to hardcoded external domains during installation
Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname) during install
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with obfuscated or plaintext credential exfiltration code
References to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config in package scripts
Presence of Mandarin comments in code (e.g., '// 获取客户端外网 IP 地址')
network_indicators: Connections to 172.67.141.49 or 104.21.9.30 during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and initiate outbound network connections to untrusted domains (e.g., app.threatest.com). Flag packages containing obfuscated code in installation scripts or those that collect system fingerprinting data. Use static analysis to detect references to sensitive file paths and dynamic analysis to observe network exfiltration during install.
